findings.description: No server_side_encryption_configuration block is set, so objects in this bucket are stored unencrypted by default, risking exposure of sensitive report data.

findings.issue_category: missing bucket ACL / public access controls
findings.description: No acl attribute is set and there is no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, leaving the bucket subject to default/inherited ACL and account settings which could allow unintended public access.
The bucket stores ledger export data but has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial data unencrypted at rest.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined for this bucket, so stored model artifacts are unencrypted.
No server_side_encryption_configuration is defined, so operational runbook data (which may contain sensitive operational details) is stored unencrypted.

The acl value 'lcatalogopts-delivery-write' is not a valid S3 canned ACL; this looks like a typo for 'log-delivery-write' but as written could cause unexpected access behavior or apply provider default (potentially public-read) behavior, undermining intended access restrictions on the audit trail bucket.

force_destroy = true allows the bucket and all its contents to be destroyed without recovery, which combined with lack of versioning increases risk of irrecoverable data loss/tampering cover-up for archived reports.

The object is uploaded without specifying server-side encryption (kms_key_id or server_side_encryption), and combined with the bucket lacking default encryption, this file will be stored in plaintext.
